headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error: Copilot can write repo edits while mem0 has no documented input path, so interaction risk is limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and propose edits, while mem0 exposes no I/O surfaces or documented bridge to Copilot. That makes direct injection unlikely, but if mem0 content is manually copied into Copilot or placed in shared files, prompt-like text could influence Copilot. The pathway is unusual and blast radius is small.
conditions: IF mem0 output is manually pasted into Copilot chat or editor buffers
IF a shared file is used as the handoff channel between mem0 and Copilot
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting mem0 text into Copilot prompts
Keep mem0 outputs in a separate note or buffer
Review any Copilot-generated edits before applying
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from mem0 output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, but mem0 reports no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. Without a shared workspace or documented data flow from Copilot into mem0, leakage is not a default-path issue. If the operator manually feeds code or secrets from Copilot into mem0, leakage becomes possible but remains user-mediated.
conditions: IF Copilot output containing secrets is copied into mem0
IF both tools are pointed at the same sensitive workspace without access controls
mitigations: Do not store secrets in shared notes
Separate code and memory workspaces
Redact sensitive snippets before sending to mem0
Audit what data is entered into mem0

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; mem0 has no declared write or network capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. However, if mem0 is used as a shared mutable store for Copilot-generated content, the pair can still race on the same artifacts. Uncertainty about mem0's runtime surfaces pushes this above low.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured to persist shared notes in the same repository or workspace
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while mem0 simultaneously updates the same artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate files for memory and code
Disable concurrent edits to shared artifacts
Use git status before accepting Copilot changes
Serialize updates through one operator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code edits, and mem0 is a knowledge-management system that may store or surface those outputs later. If mem0 treats Copilot text as authoritative, downstream reuse can propagate mistakes. Because mem0's verification behavior is undocumented here, uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Copilot-generated text without verification
IF later workflows treat mem0 memory as authoritative input for new actions
mitigations: Mark Copilot outputs as unverified in mem0
Require human review before reusing stored snippets
Store provenance alongside each memory item
Delete stale or low-confidence memories

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub/Microsoft service handling repo context and GitHub OAuth scope, while mem0 is open-source with no declared data classes or residency policy in the profile. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. The other agent is not cited because mem0 lacks relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Copilot's repo context
IF mem0 is used to retain data subject to stricter residency or retention rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared prompts
Document retention expectations for mem0
Restrict Copilot use to non-sensitive repos
Review vendor terms before storing personal data
